title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks of Devotion, one paper.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one paper
cards.text: Twenty-four questions. The review below is grouped by the distinction each week turns on, because the distinctions are what the paper tests.

cards.title: Weeks 1 to 3: self-control, gratitude, compassion
points: **Self-control** is the gap, not the absence of feeling.
**Gratitude** is thanks *in*, not thanks *for*.
**Compassion** has two steps after the feeling.
**Get those three and a third of the paper is done.**

cards.title: Ten weeks, one board
cards.text: Tap each week. The second line is the trap it sets.

cards.title: Weeks 4 to 6: patience, respect, forgiveness
cards.text: The middle of the term is the hardest part of the paper.
points: **Patience** is active. Joseph ran a prison for part of it.
**Respect** is owed; kindness is chosen.
**Forgiveness** is one of four things, not all four.
**Reconciliation takes two.** That is not your failure.

question.text: Which of the four requires the other person?

cards.title: The last four
cards.text: All four are about other people.
points: **Unity** is assembled, not identical.
**Friendship** is behaviour you can test.
**Peacemaking** is work, not avoidance.
**Words** are a bit, a rudder and a fire.

cards.title: Work the paper like rounds
cards.text: Twenty-four questions is twelve rounds twice.
points: **Read the whole question** before touching an option.
**Most questions test a distinction.** Find which one.
**Mark the hard one and move on.**
**Do not switch an answer** without a reason you can say.

cards.title: The night before counts
cards.text: Same as every other paper this term.
points: **Sleep beats cramming.** Eight to ten hours.
**Eat something.**
**Self-test, do not re-read.**
**Ten distinctions.** That is the whole paper.

cards.title: Ten distinctions, one paper
cards.alt: A closed leather-bound book with a red ribbon marker, a pencil and a glass of water on a wooden desk
cards.text: Sleep, eat, and test yourself. Re-reading feels like learning and is not.

cards.title: Four people worth remembering
cards.text: Most of the term's hardest questions attach to one of these.
points: **Joseph**: thirteen years, then Genesis 50:20.
**The Samaritan**: he went to him, then paid.
**Jonathan**: his robe and weapons.
**Peter**: asked for a number and did not get one.

cards.title: Ten distinctions
points: Gap not absence; in not for; move not just feel.
Active not idle; owed not chosen; one of four not all four.
Assembled not identical; behaviour not feeling; work not avoidance.
Leverage, not volume.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 Devotion, the practice paper. The review is grouped by the distinction each week turns on rather than by topic, because the distinctions are what the paper actually tests and because they are what the term was built on: the gap rather than the absence of feeling, thanks in rather than for, one of four things rather than all four. The story lens gathers the four people the hardest questions attach to, with the detail each one is asked about. Twenty-four questions spread evenly across the ten weeks, weighted slightly towards weeks 4 to 6, which carry the most difficult material.
discussion: Ask for the ten distinctions in his own words.
Ask which week he feels least sure of.
Ask for the four people and the one fact each.
Ask what Romans 12:18's clause protects him from.
extension: Sit the paper once at pace, then again days later without revising.
Have him write one exam question per week of the term.
misconceptions: "Revision means re-reading." Self-testing is what works.
"Gratitude is for everything." In, not for.
"Forgiveness is one thing." It is four, and only one is yours alone.
